Let’s talk about Chapter 13: The Ongoing Invitation—Living in Response.
As we come to the end of our journey together, something really important stands out. The call to “know that I am God” isn’t a one-and-done moment. It’s an ongoing invitation—one that shows up every single day, often in the smallest ways. We’re invited to pause, to listen, to trust, and to respond with our whole selves.
Imagine a young professional, swept up in the daily rush of ambition. She realized she’d been living on autopilot, just going through the motions. So, she decided to try something new—each morning, she’d ask herself, “What’s being asked of me today?” Sometimes, the answer came right away. Maybe it was a task she needed to finish, a person she could help, or even a moment to simply rest. Other days, the answer wasn’t so obvious, but just asking the question shifted her perspective. She became more attentive, more open, and ready for whatever the day might bring.
Most of us, if we’re honest, spend our days just reacting to whatever comes our way. But what if we could live from a place of deeper presence? That’s what these stories have been encouraging all along—a way of living where we notice and respond to those quiet invitations that pop up, often when we least expect them.
There’s also the story of a grandfather, looking back over a long life. He realized that the moments he treasured most weren’t about big achievements. Instead, they were found in the small acts of kindness, in listening, and in responding to the needs of others. That’s where he truly felt God’s presence—gentle, persistent, and always inviting.
Living in response doesn’t mean getting it all perfect. It’s about staying open. It’s about being willing to be led, to be changed, and to take part in the ever-unfolding story of life.
For the young professional, this daily practice brought meaning to her days. For the grandfather, surrounded by family and facing the unknown, it brought a deep sense of peace. In both their lives, the ongoing invitation became a wellspring of joy and purpose.
So, as you move forward, remember: the invitation is always there. Each day, in small and unexpected ways, you’re invited to pause, to listen, and to respond—right where you are.
